name: Nobelium

discovery.discoverer: Contested — claims by teams at Dubna, USSR and Berkeley, USA

occurrence: Does not occur naturally; produced only by particle accelerator fusion reactions, a handful of atoms at a time.
majorUses: No practical applications — pure nuclear physics research
safetyNotes: Intensely radioactive with extremely short half-lives (its most stable isotope lasts only a few minutes); never produced beyond individual atoms.
notableCharacteristics: Named after Alfred Nobel and the Nobel Institute in Sweden, and its discovery was disputed between Soviet and American research teams during Cold War-era scientific rivalry, a pattern repeated for several nearby elements.
ncertRelevance: Cold War-era discovery disputes among transfermium elements
whyHere: With a filled 5f¹⁴ subshell, nobelium is unusual among actinides for readily forming a stable +2 ion rather than the +3 typical of its neighbours, a quirk tied directly to the extra stability that filled f-subshell gives up.
didYouKnow: The naming and discovery credit for nobelium was disputed for decades between Soviet and American laboratories, part of a broader 'Transfermium Wars' that IUPAC only formally resolved for several elements in 1997.
genZNote: Caused an actual international science feud over who discovered it first. The Cold War really touched everything, apparently.
